files.title: Files
files.description: Files that tenants store through the storage module: upload, inspect, download and delete.
files.pickBody: Files always belong to one tenant. Pick a tenant to see its files and storage usage.
files.noAccessTitle: No access to this tenant's files
files.noAccessBody: Your roles do not grant files:read in this tenant. Ask a product owner for access.
files.listDescription: Newest first. Only active, unexpired files are listed.
files.emptyBody: Upload a file or change the filters.

fields.name: Name
fields.inertHelp: A blocked file type kept as an opaque attachment by the product’s content-type policy. It is only ever downloaded, never displayed.

filter.label: Filter files
filter.name: Name contains
filter.typeHelp: Exact type or a family such as image/*.
filter.labelValueHelp: JSON values (true, 42, null) match typed; other text matches as a string.

usage.title: Storage usage
usage.description: Bytes and files of this tenant's active files, compared with its effective quota.
usage.inherited: Quota inherited from the product or server default

quota.title: Storage quota
quota.description: Overrides for this tenant. Leave a field empty to inherit the product or server default.
quota.inheritHelp: Leave empty to inherit the product or server default.
quota.invalid: Enter a number of 0 or more, or leave the field empty.
quota.belowUsage: This limit is below the current usage. Existing files stay, but further uploads are refused.
quota.effectiveNote: If someone else changed the quota in the meantime, saving is refused and you can reload.
quota.bytesInfo: Once the tenant’s active files reach this size, further uploads are refused. Existing files are never deleted. 0 blocks all uploads.
quota.filesInfo: Maximum number of active files. Expired files count until the server’s purge has run. 0 blocks all uploads.

upload.title: Upload file
upload.description: The file is stored for the selected tenant. Files cannot be changed later; upload a new file instead.
upload.maxSizeUnknown: The server enforces its maximum file size.
upload.tooLarge: This file is larger than the server's limit of {{size}}.
upload.policyUnknown: The server checks size, type and quota when you upload. The allowed types are visible to product managers and platform administrators.
upload.blockedRefused: Executables, HTML, SVG and scripts are refused (checked by declared type, content and file extension).
upload.blockedInert: Executables, HTML, SVG and scripts are accepted but stored as inert application/octet-stream.
upload.typeNotAllowed: The browser reports a type that is not on the server's allow-list. The server checks the content and may refuse the file.
upload.quotaWarning: This upload probably exceeds the tenant's storage quota. The server decides.
upload.name: Display name
upload.nameHelp: Optional. Defaults to the file name.
upload.metadataHelp: Optional flat JSON object with text, number, boolean or null values, at most 64 keys.

metadataError.object: Labels must be a JSON object, for example {"kind": "invoice"}.
metadataError.values: Label values must be text, numbers, true/false or null (no nested objects or lists).

upload.expiresHelp: Optional. After this time the file is no longer visible and is removed by the purge.

errors.payload_too_largeBody: The file exceeds the server's maximum file size.
errors.unsupported_media_typeBody: The server refuses this file type. Executables, HTML, SVG and scripts are blocked, and the server may only allow certain types.
errors.quota_exceededBody: The tenant has reached its storage or file quota. Delete files or raise the quota.

upload.fileInfo: Empty files are refused. The server inspects the first bytes: a file that looks like an executable, HTML, SVG or script counts as blocked, whatever its name or declared type.
upload.metadataInfo: Keys: 1–64 characters from letters, digits and _ . : - . Text values up to 1,024 characters, 8 KiB in total. Labels appear in the audit log, so do not put secrets in them.
upload.expiresInfo: At this time the file disappears from lists and its download links stop working. The server’s purge removes it later; until then it still counts against the quota. The expiry cannot be changed after the upload.

link.title: Download link created
link.body: Anyone with this link can download the file until it expires. It cannot be revoked individually; deleting the file ends it.

delete.title: Delete file?
delete.body: {{name}} is removed for everyone and its quota is released. This cannot be undone.
delete.note: Existing download links stop working. Database backups and the audit log keep the file's name, size and checksum.

overview.title: Data overview
overview.description: Record collections, storage usage per tenant and the server's data settings.
overview.noAccessBody: Collection and storage statistics need collections:read, which product roles (owner, admin, support, viewer) grant. Tenant members can still open Records and Files for their tenant.
overview.collectionsBody: Collections across all tenants of this product.
overview.collectionsEmptyBody: Collections appear once records are written.
overview.storageBody: Usage of active files per tenant and the effective quotas.
overview.storageOffBody: Enable the storage module in the server configuration to store files.
overview.backupBody: The API reports neither backup status nor how long deleted file metadata is kept. Both are part of the server operation.
overview.quotaInfo: The effective limit: the tenant’s own quota (badge “Tenant”), otherwise the product default, otherwise the server default. Unlimited means no limit applies.

policy.title: File content-type policy
policy.description: What happens to uploads of executables, HTML, SVG and scripts in this product. Blocked files are never displayed; at most they are kept as downloads.
policy.readOnly: You can view this policy; changing it needs product:manage.
policy.modeHelp: Checked by declared type, file extension and content (including scripts that start with #!).
policy.blockedExtensionsHelp: Comma-separated, without dot, e.g. “py, rb”. Can only add to the built-in list.
policy.inertExtensionsHelp: Blocked extensions that are kept as inert attachments even when uploads are refused, e.g. “html, sh”.
policy.inertNote: Inert files are stored as application/octet-stream and downloaded as attachments with nosniff; their original type is kept for display only.
policy.loadError: The content-type policy could not be loaded.
policy.moduleOff: The storage module is not enabled on this server.
policy.modeInfo: “Refuse the upload”: the uploader gets “File type not accepted”. “Store as inert attachment”: the file is kept as application/octet-stream and can only be downloaded, never displayed. Applies to new uploads and renames; stored files stay as they are.
policy.inertExtensionsInfo: Only matters while blocked files are refused. The file name decides, even when the content is what is blocked: a script named run.sh is kept as inert if “sh” is listed; the same script named run.txt is refused.
policy.blockedInfo: The built-in list (see “Always blocked”) cannot be shortened. Entries here are blocked in addition and follow the setting “Blocked file types”. At most 100 entries.
